events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club - Hillview
events.description: Join us to practice, build, and strengthen your English-speaking skills. This is a fun, welcoming and respectful environment for adult English learners. Club meetings are held weekly and led online by a trained facilitator. Our dedicated and experienced volunteer, Patricia, leads the program and will help you build confidence in your English-speaking abilities. Please be sure to register by clicking the Register button. By providing your email address, you will receive the Zoom meeting link before the program begins.
events.blurb: Practice speaking English with fellow adult learners in a weekly conversation club led by a trained facilitator.

events.title: Spirit of '76: A Look Back at Mountain View's Bicentennial
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Learn how the "Spirit of '76" excited the residents of Mountain View as they celebrated the Bicentennial. The entire year of 1976 was filled with parades, lectures, pageants, kites, fire hydrants and more. See examples of the community coming together to learn and participate in the commemoration of the Declaration of Independence. Participants will then create artwork about how they are feeling about the 250th anniversary of American independence. We'll put the artwork together to form a "quilt" in the spirit of the Bicentennial Quilt created by a group of local women in 1976. Participants will have a chance to conduct a gallery walk to observe and reflect on the other squares in our community quilt. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear how Mountain View residents celebrated the Bicentennial with parades, pageants, and kites throughout 1976.

events.title: Murder Mystery Theater
events.description: Step into the world of a mysterious mansion where one fateful evening takes a deadly turn. You'll be given a character to play, complete with secrets, suspicions, and motives of your own. As the story unfolds, clues will be revealed and everyone becomes a suspect. Work with your fellow guests to uncover hidden secrets, piece together the evidence, and determine who committed the murder before the mystery is solved. Will you crack the case, or will the murderer get away with it? No acting experience is necessary—just bring your imagination and your detective skills! Whether you're a seasoned sleuth or simply looking for a fun and theatrical evening, everyone has a role to play in this interactive murder mystery. For Grades 9-12. Registration required.
events.blurb: Take on a character role and hunt for clues as a mysterious mansion evening turns deadly.

events.title: Afghan Cassette Archive: Stories, Sounds, and Music from Afghanistan
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join Omid Jahan, founder of the Afghan Cassette Archive (@afghancassettearchive), for a multimedia listening session exploring Afghanistan's rich musical history through rare cassette recordings, archival materials, and personal stories. The program will highlight Afghan music from different eras and communities, including recordings preserved from Afghanistan and the Afghan diaspora. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear selections from the archive, learn about the stories behind the music and artists, and view original cassette tapes and other archival materials. The session offers a unique look at Afghan history, culture, migration, and memory through the music that has traveled across generations. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear rare cassette recordings and stories from the Afghan Cassette Archive's founder Omid Jahan.

events.title: Short Story Social: "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" by Jeanette Winterson
events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. We meet virtually on the last Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List: June 25th - "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq; July 23rd - "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024; August 27th - "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez; September 24th - "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol. 45, No. 2 - available through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson.
events.blurb: Discuss Jeanette Winterson's short stories "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" with fellow readers at this virtual book club.

events.title: A Taste of History: Remembering the Wine History of Mountain View
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Before Silicon Valley, before the apricot orchards, this region was wine country. From the first vines planted at Mission Santa Clara in 1798 to more than 100 wineries operating across Santa Clara County by the 1890s, the South Bay was once one of California's most productive wine regions. Join us for a presentation by fourth-generation Mountain View resident and museum professional Julie Bly De Vere. She will present a lively look at the winemakers, vineyards, and forgotten history that shaped our local landscape long before the tech industry arrived.
events.blurb: Hear the story of Mountain View's forgotten wine industry, from Mission Santa Clara's first vines to over 100 local wineries.

events.title: Mastering Medicare: Turn Confusion into Confidence
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join us for a free, beginner-focused educational session that explains Medicare parts, enrollment timelines, and coverage options. This is an opportunity to get expert insights and clarity on how the latest Medicare updates will affect you. Whether you're new to Medicare, nearing eligibility, or already enrolled, this seminar will help you understand everything you need to know to make informed decisions about your coverage. In this comprehensive discussion, we'll explore critical topics about Medicare, such as: The ABCs (and D): Breakdown of Part A (hospital), Part B (medical), Part C (Advantage), and Part D (prescription drugs). Eligibility & Timelines: Critical enrollment windows (like the Initial Enrollment Period) to avoid late penalties. Plan Comparisons: Differences between Original Medicare, Medicare Supplement (Medigap) insurance, and Medicare Advantage. Cost Management: Review of premiums, deductibles, and strategies to lower out-of-pocket expenses. Medicare Qualifications: An overview of the eligibility requirements for Medicare, including age, disability, and any other special conditions. Cost & Penalties: Information on Medicare premiums, deductibles, co-pays, and the penalties for late enrollment. Medicare vs. Employer coverage: How Medicare works alongside employer health insurance and when to consider enrolling in Medicare if you're still working. Don't miss out on this crucial opportunity to understand how Medicare will change in 2027 and how those changes impact you. Whether you're just starting to navigate Medicare or need a refresher, this seminar is designed for everyone! This workshop will be led by Claudette G. Klein. About the Presenter: Ms. Claudette G. Klein is the owner and CEO of Klein Financial Services, a full-service, financial services firm with a primary focus on health and wealth protection, and life coverage planning. She is a Certified Financial Planner with an exemplary track record in client care, honesty, reliability, commitment and dedication. With her industry expertise, she continues to be a steady source and adviser not only of her clients, but even those who simply desire to obtain a better and clearer understanding of health and life choices that can lead to security. With a reputation as a trusted financial advisor in the Bay Area for over thirty years, Ms. Claudette Klein continues to provide unmatched service and attention. She believes in always educating current and potential clients in creating strategies for their optimal benefit, helping them understand how to make sound financial choices, assisting them with strategies that can aid in reaching their personal plans and goals, along with the attainment of peace of mind for themselves and their families.
events.blurb: Hear a beginner-focused talk on Medicare parts, enrollment timelines, and coverage options at the library.

events.title: Pages and Paws
events.description: Therapy reading dogs provide a comforting presence for children as they navigate the exciting realm of books. This initiative aims to build confidence, enhance literacy skills and instill a lifelong love for reading. Therapy dogs plan to visit on the first Friday of each month, but review our calendar to confirm dates. Limited registration is intentional to allow readers rewarding one-on-one reading time with a therapy dog. More details on your confirmed time slot and instructions will follow once you have registered. Ages 8-12.
events.blurb: Read aloud to visiting therapy dogs and build reading confidence in a relaxed library session.

events.title: Sew Sew Saturday
events.description: Need a sewing machine? The Library has sewing machines (model: Baby Lock Joy) and a serger (model: Brother 1034D) that are available for use within the Library on a drop-in basis. Whether you're working on a project or need to hem a garment, this casual, welcoming space is perfect for all skill levels. Volunteers are available to answer basic sewing questions. A limited number of supplies, such as scissors and thread, are provided. You are welcome to bring your own thread if you require a particular color. No registration required -- just bring your materials and drop in! This event is intended for adults, ages 18 and up. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Drop in to use the library's sewing machines and serger for your own hemming or sewing projects.

events.title: Seed Packets Demystified
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Do you love to look at seed catalogs and seed packets but wonder if you'd really be able to grow plants from seeds? Do you stare at the seed rack in your local nursery puzzling through what variety to plant and when you should plant it? Most seed packets contain a wealth of information to help you plant seeds of the right plant in the right place at the right time. But many of us don't bother reading the fine print, and jump straight to the planting. Join us for a lively discussion and analysis of how reading the fine print on your seed packets can help you be more successful in your garden. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn how to read seed packets and catalogs so you can actually pick and grow the right varieties.

events.title: Amplify: Gatorbotics Gear Up!
events.description: Join us for a hands-on exploration of design thinking and engineering. Learn how to interview, brainstorm, and make as we build solutions to real problems we find in the world around us. Practice hands-on engineering and learn design thinking foundational skills. Walk away with your very own prototype and a newfound excitement for engineering! Hosted by Castilleja School's Robotics Team, Gatorbotics. Recommended ages: 5-11. This event is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, a program for teens who want to share their interests and passions with an audience.
events.blurb: Interview, brainstorm, and build hands-on engineering solutions with the Gatorbotics team at the library.

events.title: Wild Fungi of California
events.description: Join Carrie Staller from Fork in the Path for an interactive hour of hands-on fun exploring the fascinating world of mushrooms! Learn how to identify mushrooms, discover chanterelles, morels, and porcini, and understand the difference between edible and poisonous varieties. We will have some specimens to touch and smell. This program is perfect for curious minds of all ages eager to learn about the natural world. About Fork in the Path: Fork in the Path offers forest-to-ocean-to-table learning programs for the adventurous of all ages across Northern California. We believe learning to forage and eating seasonal wild food is transformational. It helps us become more connected, whole, healthy, and happy. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear Carrie Staller explain how to identify mushrooms and tell edible species from poisonous ones.

events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Would you like to learn some fun songs on the ukulele? Ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan will teach participants how to play basic chords on the ukulele and lead the group in an informal performance of popular songs from the last 50 years. Bring your own uke, or use one of ours. Ages 12 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Sing and strum along with ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan in a beginner-friendly play-along session.

events.title: Amplify: Mystery of the Human Brain
events.description: Have you ever wondered what's really going on in your head? The human brain is a weird, crazy, and fascinating thing, and most people (even adults!) barely understand it. In this interactive STEM event, teens from STEM Beyond Boundaries are going to help you explore the science behind memory, learning, dreams, and other cool stuff! Ages 8-13. This event is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, a program for teens who want to share their interests and passions with an audience.
events.blurb: Join teens from STEM Beyond Boundaries for an interactive look at how your brain actually works.

events.title: Sewing with FabMo: Reversible Storage Totes
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Join us in creating reversible storage totes using upcycled fabric. This craft project will be led by FabMo volunteer, Bhanu Gomatam. This class is intended for adults, ages 18 and up. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library. Fabrics and notions for this event are provided by the Bay Area creative reuse non-profit FabMo.
events.blurb: Sew a reversible storage tote from upcycled fabric with a FabMo volunteer instructor.

events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Learn how 3D printing works and go through the full process of preparing and printing a small object. Choose a 3D model, use slicing software to set it up, and help start the print on the library's 3D printers. No prior 3D printing experience is needed but basic computer skills are expected. Ages 13 and up.
events.blurb: Learn 3D printing basics by choosing a model, slicing it, and starting your own print.

events.description: Smart Start Babytime is a special program for babies (0–2) and their caregivers that blends stories, songs, and early play with different information each week with a pediatric resident from Stanford Medical School. Caregivers will gain practical tips, build confidence, and have the opportunity to ask questions—all in a warm, supportive environment designed for your baby's earliest learning.

events.title: Cookbook Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: October's theme is "cake or pie"! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection. Don't worry; we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. Are you Team Cake or Team Pie? Both? This month we'll be showing our team spirit by making either a cake or a pie, depending on which team you're on. You can make it sweet or savory, big enough for a crowd or small enough to be held in your hand; it's up to you! Think a Swedish smörgåstårta or a savory hand pie, or one of the many, many cupcake recipes available. Or if you really are Team Both, you might consider attempting the legendary cherpumple! Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used.

events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Mountains Sing by Nguyen Phan Que Mai. Multi-generational tale of the Tran family set against the backdrop of the Vietnam War. Vivid and steeped in the language and traditions of Vietnam, the book brings to life the human costs of the conflict from the point of view of the Vietnamese people themselves, while showing the true power of kindness and hope. A perfect follow-up to The Women (our Nov. selection), which brings to life the Vietnam War from an American perspective. events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! November's book will be The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future and What We Can Do About It, by Robert Weissman. From the publisher's website: Long-time corporate accountability crusaders Robert Weissman, Public Citizen president, and Joan Claybrook, Public Citizen president emeritus, investigate how giant corporations corrupt the policy-making process to block reforms favored by overwhelming majorities of the American people, and to enrich themselves through far-reaching corporate welfare schemes. The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future And What We Can Do About It pulls back the curtain on the hidden tactics that big corporations employ to have their way in Washington, D.C. and state capitols and city halls across the nation. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Discuss The Corporation and other pressing social, economic, and political issues with fellow book club members.

events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is back for another sound healing session! Come join us! Sound and music are used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and we'll discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age Range: Adults and Seniors. Note: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. If in doubt, consult your physician before the session. The Los Gatos Library recognizes the diversity of our community and is committed to accessibility for all patrons. We strive to make every visitor feel comfortable by ensuring equal access to programs, services, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in a library program, please contact library@losgatosca.gov.
events.blurb: Lie back and let Gaby Castro-Moroder's sound healing session wash over you with music and instruments.

events.title: Facing Reality Without Losing Your Peace of Mind
events.description: We live in a time of extraordinary uncertainty and change. Political turmoil, economic instability, and troubling world events can leave us feeling anxious, overwhelmed, or helpless. Explore how to remain engaged with the world while preserving our inner peace. We may not be able to control what's happening around us, but we can learn to meet it without losing our center.
events.blurb: Hear a talk on staying engaged with a turbulent world while protecting your own inner peace.

events.title: Bug Power with Beetlelady! (Ages 6-12)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register to join in on this artistic and heroic exploration of bugs with Dr. Stephanie Dole, also known as Beetlelady! Learn all about different types of insects by interacting with live bugs, and invent your own superhero bug with a fun drawing activity! This class is for ages 6-12, and registration is required (registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event).
events.blurb: Meet live insects and invent your own bug superhero with Beetlelady in this hands-on drawing activity.

events.title: Free Repairs with Repair Café
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you need help repairing something? Repair Café Silicon Valley will be at the library offering free repairs on household items such as toasters, lamps, radios, clothing, bikes, and more. Limit two items per household; last repairs accepted at 2:30 PM. Visit repaircafesv.org for more information about their mission and to see when other events are scheduled.
events.blurb: Bring a broken toaster, lamp, radio, or bike and get it fixed free by Repair Café Silicon Valley volunteers.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Felicia's Journey by William Trevor. A story of lost opportunities, naivety, and misplaced hopes of an Irish girl who leaves Ireland to find her boyfriend in England. By one of Ireland's most admired writers. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Discuss Felicia's Journey, William Trevor's story of an Irish girl chasing lost hopes in England, with the group.

events.title: Cafecito Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: This book club reads exclusively Spanish books and meets on the 2nd Thursday of every month from 10-11 AM in the library's conference room (1st Floor). Este club de lectura lee libros exclusivamente en español y se reúne el segundo jueves de cada mes de 10 a 11 a.m. en la sala de conferencias de la biblioteca (primer piso).
events.blurb: Talk through a Spanish-language book with other readers in the library's first-floor conference room.

events.description: Take some time out of your afternoon to imagine and create! Join us for a crafty activity in the Children's Room. (Previously known as Tinker Tuesday.) This program is geared towards children ages 3 through ~10. This program takes place on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 pm in the Children's Room.

events.title: Psychic Readings
events.description: Gather your friends for a pre-Halloween evening of psychic readings with Psychic Medium Janis Manacsa and Sound Practitioner Julie Kalua. Experience live gallery readings, opening and closing sound baths, and the mystery of the season. October 30, 6:30–9 p.m. at East West Bookshop. Limited to 20 guests.

events.title: Seated Sound Bath • Friday, October 16th • 7:00pm - Buy 1 & Bring a Friend!
events.description: Seated Sound Bath - One ticket admits you + one guest at no additional charge. During this session, Julie will create a serene soundscape using singing bowls, gongs, and other therapeutic instruments, enveloping you in waves of sound that resonate through your entire being.
events.blurb: Sit back and let Julie's singing bowls and gongs wash over you in a calming sound bath, friend included free.

events.title: Existence Beyond Death: With Dr. Seng-Beng Ho - Friday November 6th at 7pm
events.description: Explore near-death experiences, reincarnation, and the UFO connection with author and cognitive scientist Dr. Seng-Beng Ho. An evening of research, reported experiences, and questions about consciousness and reality, followed by Q&A. November 6, 7–8:30 p.m. | $25.
events.blurb: Hear cognitive scientist Dr. Seng-Beng Ho discuss near-death experiences, reincarnation, and consciousness, then join the Q&A.

events.title: Seed Library Tabling
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a fun-filled craft in the lobby that promotes the Los Gatos Seed Library. Learn more about community stewardship and how to collect and donate seeds, along with why native plants are so important to our community health and wellbeing.
events.blurb: Make a craft in the library lobby while learning how to collect and donate seeds for the Los Gatos Seed Library.

events.title: Park-It Market
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join the team from West Valley Community Services for their twice-monthly Park-It Market. On the second and fourth Thursday of each month, WVCS offers free access to food including fresh produce, meat, dairy products, dry goods and canned food.
events.blurb: Pick up free fresh produce, meat, dairy, and canned goods from West Valley Community Services.

events.title: Adventure Skeletons TTRPG
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a Halloween-themed role-playing game, Adventure Skeletons. Players will make their way through the haunted Spirit Halloween to... Liberate their skeleton kin? Take over the world? Go on vacation? The choice is yours!
events.blurb: Roll dice through a Halloween-themed tabletop adventure as skeletons navigating a haunted Spirit Halloween.

events.title: Judi Oyama: To Be Seen / Not Heard Exhibition Opening Celebration & Free Admission Day
events.venue: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
events.description: Our newest rotating exhibition, Judi Oyama: To Be Seen / Not Heard officially opens to the public on October 31st, 2026! Join us at the museum and celebrate this exhibition's opening day with us!
events.blurb: See Judi Oyama's new exhibition on its opening day and get in free at the museum.

events.title: Full Immersion Comfort Sound Bath Saturday
events.description: Three people. 180 degrees of sound. A deeper, more intimate container for the Full Immersion experience — where the sound has more space to move and your nervous system has more room to fully arrive.
events.blurb: Lie back in a small group and let layered sound wash over you from three directions.

events.title: World War II Japanese American Veteran Monument: Dedication & Gathering
events.venue: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
events.description: Join us in honoring the World War II Japanese American veterans who fought in World War II with a community gathering and monument dedication.
events.blurb: Gather for the dedication of a new monument honoring Japanese American WWII veterans at the museum.

events.title: Cars & Croissants on the Row
events.description: October 18, 2026. Join us on Sunday, October 18th from 9 AM-12 PM for the 100 | OCT Cars and Croissants on The Row! Experience one of the world's premier exotic car gatherings, featuring an impressive display of supercars, luxury vehicles, and exotic marques from renowned manufacturers. Whether you're a dedicated car enthusiast or simply looking for a fun morning out, enjoy the opportunity to see incredible vehicles up close, connect with fellow automotive fans, and take in the vibrant atmosphere of Santana Row. This event is free to attend. We look forward to seeing you on the Row!
events.blurb: Walk Santana Row and check out supercars, luxury vehicles, and exotic marques on display.

events.title: Día de Los Muertos Celebration
events.description: November 1, 2026. Join the festivities as Santana Row hosts a very special tribute to Día de Los Muertos on Sunday, November 1st! The holiday is a time to remember loved ones that have passed, while we embrace our eternal connections. This is a free community event featuring face painting, Catrina and Catrin meet & greets, mariachi music, crafts, and a pop-up market. Entertainment Schedule: 10:30 AM – 10 PM: Brunch at Zazil & contribute to the Community Ofrendas (Altars); 12 – 5 PM: Cultural Pop-Up Market; 12 – 3 PM: Día de los Muertos Catrina Photo Ops in Oak Tree Lounge (by Blue Bottle Coffee); 12 – 3 PM: Face Painting in Santana Row Park; 1 – 3 PM: Mariachi & Dance Performances in Santana Row Park; 3 – 4:30 PM: Mariachi & Face Painting at El Jardín Tequila Bar; 4:30 – 6 PM: Mariachi at Zazil.
events.blurb: Join Santana Row's Día de Los Muertos tribute with face painting and community festivities honoring loved ones.

events.title: Trick-or-Treat the Row Halloween Family Festival

This event is free and open to the public. Trick-or-Treat stops to be announced soon.

events.description: Join us for an exciting, informative program about bats! Recommended for ages 5-12, but all ages are welcome. events.title: Vietnamese Storytime & Craft
events.description: Thân mời các bé cùng cha mẹ hoặc người chăm sóc bé đến tham dự Giờ Kể Chuyện và làm thủ công bằng tiếng Việt tại Thư Viện Evergreen! Chúng ta sẽ cùng nhau nghe kể chuyện, hát ca và tham gia các hoạt động vui nhộn giúp bé phát triển kỹ năng ngôn ngữ và niềm yêu thích đọc sách từ sớm. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Chương trình phù hợp với trẻ em ở mọi độ tuổi và là dịp tuyệt vời để cả gia đình cùng học hỏi, vui chơi và kết nối. Không cần đăng ký trước. Hãy rủ bạn bè cùng tham gia nhé! Join us for a fun and engaging Vietnamese Storytime and Craft at Evergreen Library! Children and their parents or caregivers will enjoy stories, songs, and playful activities in Vietnamese that help build early language and literacy skills. Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! This program is perfect for children of all ages and offers a wonderful opportunity for families to learn, play, and grow together. No registration is required. Bring your friends to join us!
events.attendanceNote: · All participants will need a storytime ticket. Tickets are limited and available at the Information Desk 30-minutes before the program.
events.blurb: Bring kids to hear Vietnamese stories, sing songs, and make a craft at Evergreen Library.

events.description: Learn to use a computer with confidence! In this hands-on course, you'll learn the fundamentals of computers including how to use the keyboard and mouse, browse the Internet, use email, create documents, and more. Develop useful skills for school, work, and everyday life. Ideal for beginners. No prior experience required! Free. Bilingual. ¡Aprende a usar la computadora con confianza! En este curso práctico aprenderás los fundamentos de la computación, incluyendo el uso del teclado y el mouse, navegación por Internet, correo electrónico, creación de documentos y más. events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help - Trợ Giúp Kỹ Năng Máy Tính Bằng Tiếng Việt
events.description: This event is offered in Vietnamese. Are you or your loved ones struggling with using a smartphone, downloading apps, or making video calls to see the family? Come join our Free One-on-One Tech Mentor Support sessions. We can help you with: Basic help for smartphones, tablets, and computers; Downloading and using everyday apps; Making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet) to stay connected; Exploring AI tools and answering your AI questions / concerns; Navigating our library website and wonderful digital resources. Note: Our support is focused on basic technology questions. Drop-ins are accepted. How to make an appointment: Priority will be given to patrons with appointments, so please book yours today! Call us at: (408) 808-3060. Email Rebecca Quan at: Rebecca.quan@sjlibrary.org. Có cô chú hay ông bà, cha mẹ mình đang gặp chút khó khăn khi dùng điện thoại thông minh, tải ứng dụng, hay muốn gọi video để gặp con cháu mà chưa biết cách không ạ? Quý vị hãy ghi danh cho người thân để họ tham gia chương trình Hỗ trợ Công nghệ 1-kèm-1 miễn phí. Chúng tôi sẽ hướng dẫn tận tình các kỹ năng sau: Sử dụng điện thoại, máy tính bảng và máy tính cơ bản; Cách tải và sử dụng các ứng dụng hữu ích; Cách gọi video (Zoom, Google Meet...) để kết nối với gia đình; Giải đáp các thắc mắc về AI mới; Cách tra cứu trang web của Thư Viện San Jose và sử dụng các tài nguyên số bổ ích. Lưu ý: Chương trình tập trung hỗ trợ các câu hỏi và thao tác công nghệ cơ bản. Chào đón quý vị tới gặp nhân viên thư viện nếu có câu hỏi đơn giản. Cách thức ghi danh: Xin ghi danh đặt hẹn trước (thư viện sẽ ưu tiên cho người có lịch hẹn): Gọi điện thoại: (408) 808-3060. Hoặc gửi email cho cô Rebecca Quan: rebecca.quan@sjlibrary.org. Hosted by Evergreen Branch. #dsb Digital Skills

events.title: Berryessa Book Club
events.description: Join the Berryessa Book Club on the third Friday of the month for a fun and engaging literary discussion. In October, around Halloween, we will read Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus by Mary Shelley. Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus is one of the best-known works of English literature. The novel has set a path for modern Western literature, particularly for the Romantic movement and the genre of Gothic horror. The story of Doctor Frankenstein and his monstrous creature has profoundly influenced popular culture and, 200 years after its publication, has become more relevant than ever. The list of books by month (September-June) is available upon request. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Discuss Mary Shelley's Frankenstein with fellow readers at the Berryessa Book Club's monthly meeting.

events.title: ESL Workforce Development Workshop - Day 3: Professional Communication & Workplace Expectations
events.description: Join us for a five-session workshop designed for ESL learners who want to strengthen their workplace communication skills. In addition, participants will develop basic digital skills by learning how to use Google Workspace tools (Docs, Slides, and Drive) and Canva to create professional documents and presentations that can support job searches, interviews, and career advancement. Participants should be able to communicate in basic English (speaking, reading, and writing). Workshop topic: Professional Communication & Workplace Expectations. This is a free program. Registration is required. Talleres de Desarrollo Laboral para Estudiantes Hispanos de ESL. Acompáñenos a este taller de cinco sesiones diseñado para estudiantes de inglés (ESL) que desean fortalecer sus habilidades de comunicación en el entorno laboral. Además, los participantes desarrollarán habilidades digitales básicas al aprender a utilizar las herramientas de Google Workspace (Docs, Slides y Drive) y Canva para crear documentos y presentaciones profesionales que les apoyen en la búsqueda de empleo, las entrevistas y el desarrollo de su carrera profesional. Los participantes deben tener la capacidad de comunicarse en inglés a un nivel básico (hablar, leer y escribir). Tema del taller: Comunicación Profesional y Expectativas en el Lugar de Trabajo. Este programa es gratuito. Es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice workplace communication and build digital skills with Google Workspace and Canva in this ESL workshop.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades TK-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a trained volunteer or staff member. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our volunteers will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Rose Garden Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating students.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first come, first served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating students.
events.blurb: Pair up with a trained volunteer to read one-on-one and build reading confidence.

events.title: Santa Teresa Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: This leadership and volunteer service group for teens ages 13-18 meets in person on the third Friday of each month from 4-5 PM in the Community Room. Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. Our monthly meetings include snacks; teen volunteer opportunities; updates on upcoming library teen programs and new materials; games and activities. Join us and represent the teen community at your local library! Please visit the Teens Reach: Community Service webpage for more information. Create your online volunteer account by clicking "Sign Me Up" under Santa Teresa Branch Library.
events.blurb: Join teens building leadership and volunteer experience through the Teens Reach youth council meeting.

events.title: STEM: Mathema Adventures: A D&D-Inspired Math Games Program for Kids
events.description: Join us for a Dungeons & Dragons session that will be built around the magical world of Mathema, where math problems are as numerous as the creatures you will encounter in this interactive and immersive adventure that will help young patrons practice math. events.title: Delphian Lectures: Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties
events.description: A lecture series presented by the Delphian Study Club - providing the opportunity for lifelong learning and friendship via lectures and events. The current series: "Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties" will focus on the history and engineering of musical instruments and the composers who wrote for the instruments. Specific Lecture Topics: September 18, 2026 - Introductory class with series guest lecturer, Debora Rosengaus - Get ready, 'cause here we go! October 2, 2026 - Meet the Piano; October 16, 2026 - Meet the Strings; November 6, 2026 - Meet the Guitar; November 20, 2026 - Meet the Brass; December 4, 2026 - Meet the Woodwinds; January 15, 2027 - Meet the Percussion; February 5, 2027 - Meet the Conductors; February 19, 2027 - Meet the Unusual Instruments; March 5, 2027 - Meet the Bach Family; April 2, 2027 - Meet the Mozart Family; April 16, 2027 - Meet the Schumann Family; May 7, 2027 - Meet the Mendelssohn Siblings; May 21, 2027 - Meet the Strauss Family, Waltz Kings. This series will be presented by Deborah Martínez Rosengaus, a versatile Mezzo Soprano who has studied Opera, Theater, Music and Dance, and has toured internationally, with a variety of musical ensembles in concert halls such as: Suntory Hall in Tokyo, The Center for Performing Arts in Beijing, Disney Hall with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, The Lincoln Center and Carnegie Hall. She has given recitals in Mexico and across the United States, giving voice to her research into the lesser-known Art Songs of great Classical composers. Ms. Rosengaus holds a Master of Music Degree from the Manhattan School of Music, where she studied with international opera diva Mignon Dunn, and a Bachelor's Degree from the University of Southern California Thornton School of Music. She is the recipient of several awards including the Schoenfeld Award from the Holt Memorial Scholarship Competition and 1st place in the Pacific Musical Society Competition. She has also performed in Master classes with Karen Morrow and Luana Devol, and is a featured vocalist on several independent film soundtracks. She is known for her exciting, high-energy performances and for creating memorable and endearing characters such as the role of Principessa Louling under the baton of Bruno Riggacci in the world premiere of his one-act opera "Dodici personaggi in cerca di voce." She has received critical acclaim for her interpretation of Jo in Mark Adamo's Little Women and was nominated for a Theater Bay Area Award for the role of Ruth in Pirates of Penzance. Guests are always welcome and encouraged. Free. No registration required.

If you registered successfully, you will get a registration confirmation email with a link to pick your choice of time for this Saturday's program. Each session is one hour (15-30 minutes for interviewing + 30-45 minutes for helpful feedback). The one-hour time slots to pick from are as follows: 10:00 - 11:00 am or 11:00 am - 12:00 pm. Please note that there is a 5-minute buffer to include any setup and help prevent any overlap between appointments. Resumes and job position descriptions are reviewed in advance. Please email documents to Jeff.Tibayan@sjlibrary.org by 5 PM on the Thursday before your Saturday session. This gives Daniel enough time to prepare job interview materials. Registration Information: Please register using a valid email address. Double-check that your email address is correct before confirming your registration.
events.blurb: Meet one-on-one with a coach for resume feedback and a mock job interview.

events.title: ESL Workforce Development Workshop - Day 3: Professional Communication & Workplace Expectations
events.description: Join us for a five-session workshop designed for ESL learners who want to strengthen their workplace communication skills. In addition, participants will develop basic digital skills by learning how to use Google Workspace tools (Docs, Slides, and Drive) and Canva to create professional documents and presentations that can support job searches, interviews, and career advancement. Participants should be able to communicate in basic English (speaking, reading, and writing). Workshop topic: Professional Communication & Workplace Expectations. This is a free program. Registration is required. Talleres de Desarrollo Laboral para Estudiantes Hispanos de ESL. Acompáñenos a este taller de cinco sesiones diseñado para estudiantes de inglés (ESL) que desean fortalecer sus habilidades de comunicación en el entorno laboral. Además, los participantes desarrollarán habilidades digitales básicas al aprender a utilizar las herramientas de Google Workspace (Docs, Slides y Drive) y Canva para crear documentos y presentaciones profesionales que les apoyen en la búsqueda de empleo, las entrevistas y el desarrollo de su carrera profesional. Los participantes deben tener la capacidad de comunicarse en inglés a un nivel básico (hablar, leer y escribir). Tema del taller: Comunicación Profesional y Expectativas en el Lugar de Trabajo. Este programa es gratuito. Es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice workplace communication and build Google Workspace and Canva skills in this ESL workforce workshop.

events.title: ELL / ELL Conversation Club for Mandarin Speakers
events.description: Join us for an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! The presenter is bilingual in both English and Chinese Mandarin. Other English language learners are welcome. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice English conversation with other adult learners at this Mandarin-speaker ELL club.

events.title: Spooky Halloween Science
events.description: "Spooky Halloween Science" is a hands-on STEAM workshop for children ages 5 to 12, presented by Science Smart Kids. Children will make "witches' brew" that will bubble and fizz due to a fun chemical reaction, and make bright green and stretchy "Ogre Boogers" (slime) to take home. You won't want to miss Halloween storytime, as well! For ages 5 to 12. Younger participants must be accompanied by a participating parent/caregiver. Attendance is limited. Participants must pick up a ticket at the Information Desk. Tickets will be available 1 hour prior to the program's start time. The child must be present to receive a ticket. This program has been generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.
events.attendanceNote: Attendance is limited. Participants must pick up a ticket at the Information Desk. Tickets will be available 1 hour prior to the program's start time. Child must be present to receive a ticket.
events.blurb: Mix a bubbling witches' brew and stretch homemade slime at this hands-on science workshop for kids.

events.title: Baby Lapsit Storytime
events.description: This program is for babies that are not yet walking confidently, and their caregivers. Baby Lapsit invites newborns, young infants, and their caregivers to learn together and strengthen their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! Some special toys and the Storytime librarian will join in the fun, giving babies and parents time to connect. Baby Lapsit Storytime: 2:00 pm - 2:25 pm; Stay & Play: 2:25 pm - 2:55 pm. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free, with limited capacity. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bond with your pre-walking baby through songs, rhymes, bounces, and books at this lapsit storytime.

events.title: Saturday Showtime: Frida
events.description: Celebrate National Hispanic Heritage Month with the 2002 biopic Frida. This Oscar-winning film follows Mexican surrealist artist Frida Kahlo from a bus accident during her teenage years through her growth as an artist with unique vision and style. Frida Kahlo's radical and revolutionary persona is brought to life on screen including her marriage to Diego Rivera, scandalous affairs, political activism and uncompromising personality. Rated R; 123 minutes. Movie trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-CTM7FcY1LE Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Watch the Oscar-winning biopic Frida in celebration of Hispanic Heritage Month.

events.title: Hillview - Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class
events.description: Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills for free! This class meets in person at Hillview Branch Library and is led by a certified English instructor in collaboration with Overfelt Adult Education Center at no cost. Starts: August 15, 2026; Meets: Saturdays; Instructor: Annalisa Hernandez. Free. Aprende lectura, escritura, expresión oral y comprensión auditiva de manera gratuita. Esta clase se reúne en persona en la Biblioteca Hillview Branch y está dirigida por una instructora certificada de inglés en colaboración con el Centro de Educación para Adultos Overfelt, sin costo alguno. Inicio: 15 de agosto de 2026; Días: sábados; Instructora: Annalisa Hernández. Gratis.
events.blurb: Learn reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills for free in this ESL class at Hillview Library led by a certified instructor.

events.title: Cozy Paws: Toys for Shelter Dogs
events.description: Join us for a family-friendly, volunteer drop-in event where participants of all ages can braid or sew used, machine-washed clothing into dog toys for local shelters! Reminder: This is NOT a craft to take home. All dog toys are created for donation to local shelters! If you are here to Volunteer Away Your Fines, please be sure to bring your library card and sign in so that we can track your hour(s). We'll waive your fines at a rate of $20 per hour. Details and Requirements: Anyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardian. No experience or special skills necessary. Training and supplies will be provided.
events.blurb: Drop in with the family to braid and sew used clothing into toys donated to local animal shelters.

events.title: 1 on 1 Tech Assistance
events.description: Do you need to brush up on your computer skills? Whether you need assistance putting together a Word document, Excel spreadsheet, or PowerPoint presentation, submitting an online job application or other government document, or learning a new online tool, our experienced and dedicated tech tutors can help! Current Weekly Schedule: Wednesdays at 4:00 PM (in the Internet Cafe); Thursdays at 11 AM - assistance available in English or Mandarin Chinese (in the Group Study Room); Saturdays at 10 AM (in the Group Study Room). How to attend: Participants are encouraged to pre-register; however, drop-ins are also considered.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or online forms from a tech tutor at Willow Glen Library.

events.title: STEM Saturday: Be a Scientist
events.description: Join us as the group Be a Scientist takes us on a journey that explores the exciting worlds of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Each week we will explore a subject through a unique activity that sparks curiosity and brings the topic to life through making and experimenting. Each week of STEM brings a new set of tasks to challenge us. Sessions are not related, so participants should register for each session they wish to attend. Registration is required. This series of programs is supported by our Friends of the Pearl Avenue Library.
events.blurb: Join Be a Scientist for a hands-on STEM activity exploring science, technology, engineering, or math at Pearl Avenue Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Throughout this 30-minute session, our trained volunteer or a staff member of the library will not only read to your kids but also engage with them using music, felts and finger plays. As a result of participating in Reading to Children, your child will develop imagination and love of books and reading. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Bring your kids to a 30-minute reading session led by a trained volunteer at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Language and Culture Swap
events.description: ¿Hablas español y quieres aprender inglés? Speak English and want to learn Spanish? Build community with people from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. Everyone has something to contribute! Construye comunidad con personas de diferentes antecedentes lingüísticos y culturales. ¡Todos tienen algo que aportar! In this program, Spanish-proficient participants with limited English skills will share their linguistic and cultural knowledge with English-proficient participants with limited Spanish skills and vice-versa to create a mutually enriching learning experience. En este programa, los participantes con dominio del español y habilidades limitadas en inglés compartirán sus conocimientos lingüísticos y culturales con participantes con dominio del inglés y habilidades limitadas en español, y viceversa, para crear una experiencia de aprendizaje mutuamente enriquecedora. Free. Registration requested but not required.
events.blurb: Swap English and Spanish conversation with neighbors building cross-cultural friendships at Alum Rock Library.

events.title: OneInMath: Math Program for Grades K-3
events.description: Join us for a free math program for kindergarten to 3rd grade students to learn basic arithmetic, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division from one-digit to four-digit numbers. It is taught by trained high school students. The focus is to build confidence and love for Math in young students. This program is suitable for children in grades K-3. Registration and Data Privacy: Registration is required. Visit the One In Math website to register. You may be asked to provide personal information to sign up. Please review One In Math's Privacy Policy before registering.
events.blurb: Watch students in grades K-3 practice arithmetic with trained high schoolers at Tully Library's free OneInMath program.

events.title: Saturday STEM: Potato Clocks!
events.description: Join us for Saturday STEM! Kids will explore a fun STEM activity focused on the theme of the day. Explore the exciting worlds of chemistry and electronic circuitry... Our volunteer Kimmie will explain the principles behind electrochemical battery power and kids will have a chance to build a functioning digital clock powered entirely by a potato! This interactive program is appropriate for elementary and middle school students. Space is limited to 15 participants, and tickets will be available at the Front Desk one hour before the event begins to secure a spot. Tickets and supplies are available on a first-come, first-served basis. We hope to see you there!
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited to 15 participants, and tickets will be available at the Front Desk one hour before the event begins to secure a spot. Tickets and supplies are available on a first come, first served basis.
events.blurb: Build a potato-powered battery and learn the chemistry and circuitry behind electrochemical power with kids.

events.title: Reading Buddies with Kristina
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Children in grades K to 5 will discover the joy of reading while improving their reading skills through practice with Kristina on Saturdays. Our reading buddy will listen to children and help them build confidence in their ability to read. They will ask questions about the books being read to encourage reading comprehension. Children will enjoy one-on-one interaction with Kristina who has been trained to create a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers. Reading Buddies are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.attendanceNote: Reading Buddies are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.blurb: Bring a child in grades K-5 to read aloud with Kristina and build reading confidence one on one.

events.title: Citizenship Study Group (In-person)
events.description: Free. Register for reminders. Drop-ins welcome. What We Do: Outline the naturalization process; Review civics (2008 & 2025); Practice reading & writing; Analyze the interview questions; Provide references & resources; Mock interviews (depending on availability). Due to legal reasons, we cannot help you fill out the application, but we can direct you to the proper services. The class is offered in English with limited Vietnamese and Spanish assistance. For additional resources, please review our Citizenship and Immigration page.
events.blurb: Sit in on a citizenship study group covering civics review, interview practice, and naturalization process guidance.

events.title: Sparksteam Robotics Program: Learn, Build, Code, Play with Robots
events.description: The Sparksteam Robotics Program introduces elementary school students (grades 2–5) to the exciting world of robotics and coding through fun, hands-on activities. Students will learn the basics of building and programming robots using LEGO robotics kits. Sparksteam will provide robotics kits and laptops that will be used for programming the robots. We just need enthusiastic kids! The program conducted by the San José Public Library is not affiliated, sponsored, or endorsed by LEGO Education or The LEGO Group. LEGO is a trademark of the LEGO Group of companies which does not sponsor, authorize or endorse this site.
events.blurb: Build and program LEGO robots with hands-on guidance in this elementary-grade robotics program.

events.title: Friends of the Cambrian Branch Library Book Sale
events.description: Choose from a large selection of donated books, media, and specialty items. Proceeds go toward funding library programs, books, and supplies. Come support your local library branch and find new literary treasures for yourself. The Friends of the Cambrian Branch Library host a quarterly Book Sale in the library's community room to raise funds for the Cambrian Branch Library. Check out the large selection of books for all ages and interests to support your local library. Special $5 Bag Sale from 1:30 pm to 2:00 pm. Select a grocery bag-full of books for $5. Selection begins at 1:30 pm after the book sale. Accepted payment is cash, check, or Zelle.
events.blurb: Browse donated books, media, and specialty items at the Cambrian Branch Library's fundraising book sale.

events.title: Everyone Can Create: Let's Make Logos
events.description: Kids will learn to think like a graphic designer. They will brainstorm the design process, and create their very own logo. We will learn to use Tayasui Sketches, a beginner drawing application for the iPad. This is a fun class for students to bring their imagination and ideas to life, all while learning to use good design principles. All materials needed will be provided. No registration required. Free, with limited capacity. Sign-in sheet is available at the Info desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need to sign in to attend. Appropriate for ages 7 to 15. Participants are required to bring their own headphones / earbuds.
events.blurb: Sketch and design your own logo on an iPad using Tayasui Sketches at Edenvale Library.

events.title: Almaden Branch Library's 20th Anniversary & Harvest Festival Celebration
events.description: Join us as the Almaden Branch Library and Community Center celebrate 20 years of service in the neighborhood as a part of this year's annual Harvest Festival with the City of San José's Parks, Recreation & Neighborhood Services Department. Opening Remarks: Jimmy Panetta, U.S. Representative, California's 19th Congressional District; Gail Pellerin, California State Assemblymember, District 28; George Casey, San José City Councilmember, District 10; Jon Cicirelli, Director of Parks, Recreation and Neighborhood Services, City of San José; Jill Bourne, City Librarian, San José Public Library. Live Entertainment, Activities, Giveaway: Live music from the Castillero Middle School Orchestra; A cultural dance performance by Jayendra Kalakendra; A Cool Bubble Party, balloon artist, and a calligrapher; Vendor booths & kids' bounce house; A Haunted Hallway & Pumpkin Patch (ticket purchase required*); Games, face painting & crafts for all ages (ticket purchase required*); Treats & refreshments; Book giveaways & more. *Ticket prices will vary. Pricing available at the event. This program is generously sponsored, in part, by the Friends of the Almaden Library and the SJPL Foundation's Pat Dando Endowment. Share Your Story: Share your Almaden Branch story by telling us about a favorite memory, experience, or special moment. Request ADA accommodations for this event.
events.attendanceNote: A Haunted Hallway & Pumpkin Patch (ticket purchase required*) Games, face painting & crafts for all ages (ticket purchase required*) *Ticket prices will vary. Pricing available at the event.
events.blurb: Celebrate Almaden Branch Library's 20th anniversary with Harvest Festival activities and remarks from local officials.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. They are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K to 3 and will be held in the Children's area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your child to Alviso Library for one-on-one reading time with a volunteer.

events.title: College Readiness
events.description: In this program, get personal assistance with basic college readiness and advice when preparing yourself to further your education. Our knowledgeable volunteer will provide free, one-on-one tutoring at the library. These in-person sessions can help strengthen your knowledge, goals, letter writing, and test-taking skills to improve your college application and set you up for future success! Topics may also include: ACT & SAT test prep; general high school or college advice on: choosing classes, joining clubs, creating study plans or career goals, how to network with teachers or professors, choosing and prepping for summer opportunities, resume & job application advice / help; College Application Process: general questions, timeline advice, college selection, essay review, interview practice; Financial Aid: Basic info on types of aid available and how it can help. Please note that no specific financial advice will be given outside of general information and best practices. Space is limited to keep interactions more personalized for each individual. Registration is recommended for a guaranteed spot.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited to keep interactions more personalized for each individual.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one college readiness tutoring from a knowledgeable volunteer to strengthen your prep and planning.

Sessions are 30 minutes and appointments are highly encouraged, though drop-ins can be taken on a first-come, first-served basis if times are available. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime. San José Public Library Storytimes are developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

events.title: 3D Design & Printing
events.description: Learn to design in Tinkercad and see your creation come to life with our 3D printer! Each class introduces a new technique in Tinkercad or other 3D design tools. Participants will have the opportunity to create a project which will be printed out for pickup later. Classes are on the second Saturday of the month, except in June and October, when they will be on the third Saturday. No experience necessary. Participants do not have to participate in all sessions. May 9 - Magnets (negative space + combining shapes); June 20 - Stamps (scribble tool + rotation); July 11 - Standing Sculptures (alignment + supports); August 8 - Free Choice (importing and editing outside designs); September 12 - Hinged Shapes (hinges + print in place); October 17 - Lithophanes; November 14 - Cookie Cutters (2D to 3D conversion); December 12 - Snowflakes (codeblocks for generating designs). Appropriate for ages 8+ - younger children will need to be accompanied by an adult to assist them with their design. One dedicated helper needed per child under 8. Space is limited - tickets will be available at the desk 30 minutes before the program begins. One ticket per participant; helpers/spectators do not need a ticket. Each person participating must be present in order to receive their ticket. There are two sessions, one at 3:30 and one at 4:45 pm, to help with crowding. These sessions are identical.

events.title: TeenHQ: Cupcake Lamps
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Create a colorful cupcake lamp with Mod Podge and tissue paper. Each teen will receive a white 3D-printed cupcake to customize, along with an LED light puck and one set of batteries. Cupcakes will be a little larger than shown and hide the light puck inside when finished. Pre-registration is required to reserve your cupcake and LED light puck. We will not hold a waitlist. If you are unable to participate after pre-registering, please unregister immediately so another person can take your spot. If all spots are taken, please check back regularly to see if someone has unregistered. Pre-registration will close 4 hours prior to the start of the program. Middle and high schoolers are welcome to join TeenHQ for a special birthday-themed craft to celebrate TeenHQ turning 10! TeenHQ was established in 2016.
events.blurb: Build and decorate a 3D-printed cupcake lamp with LED lights and tissue paper at King Library.

events.title: Bay Area Games Day
events.description: Come learn how to play a new board game, or bring an old favorite! Bay Area Games Day is a full day of convention-style open gaming that has been happening at the library since 1998. We play mostly more recent hobbyist games, but also classic strategy games such as Catan or Pandemic, and family and party games. We welcome newcomers to hobby gaming and families with kids. https://groups.io/g/gamesday For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.description: Need a calming corner on a busy Saturday? Stop by and visit Sensor E, an organization that fosters unity despite differences through sensory play. For children and tweens and their families. Generously sponsored by the Friends of Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Visit Sensor E's sensory play stations for a calming break with your kids.

events.title: LWV - 14 State Propositions
events.description: There are important issues on the November 2026 Ballot. These include 14 state measures and the SCC Transit Tax Measure. The League of Women Voters will be presenting a non-partisan Pro & Con Session to explain this year's propositions and help voters make informed decisions. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Hear the League of Women Voters break down the pros and cons of the 14 state ballot measures.

events.title: Home Remodel Workshop
events.description: This workshop is designed for homeowners considering a remodel, addition, ADU, or major home reconfiguration who may be unsure where to begin. This workshop will help participants clarify their household needs and project priorities; understand the components of a complete project budget; identify early permitting and feasibility questions; understand the roles of designers, engineers, contractors, and other professionals; and prepare better questions before signing agreements or investing heavily in design and construction. Attendees will use a guided workbook to apply each step to their own proposed projects.
events.blurb: Sit in on tips for clarifying your remodel, addition, or ADU project priorities before you begin.

events.title: Dreaming with Your Eyes Open: Double Bill
events.description: Come join us in the beautiful Milpitas Library for an afternoon of surreal movies exploring themes of creation. At 2:00 PM, we will be showing The Blood of A Poet (Le Sang d'un poète): an artist's dreamy, bizarre trip through his subconscious and one of my favorite films! (This movie is in French with English subtitles.) At 3:00 PM, we will be showing David Lynch's nightmarish cult classic Eraserhead. This program is part of the Surreal Film Series! Previous events in the series: August 29: Alice in Wonderland and Fantastic Planet. September 19: The Exterminating Angel and Synecdoche, New York.
events.blurb: Watch The Blood of a Poet unfold on screen as a surreal journey through the subconscious.

events.title: History of the US-Canada Trade War
events.description: Join Santa Clara University Teaching Professor Greg Wigmore in partnership with the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW for a talk about the history of the Canada-U.S. trade war. This talk will touch on Canadian Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau's meeting in Washington in 1969 and will also explain why relations between the two countries are more strained than they've been for over a century, with boycotts, insults, talk of annexation, and an escalating trade war. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear Professor Greg Wigmore trace the history of the Canada-U.S. trade war back to 1969.

events.title: Adult & Teen Crafternoon: Monster Miniatures
events.description: The Adult & Teen Crafternoon occurs every month on the third Saturday, from 3 - 4:30 PM. Patrons ages 13+ are invited to take part in a different craft or art project each month. You are welcome to drop in at any time, but please note most projects will take over 30 minutes to complete. We hope to see you there! October's craft is Monster Miniatures! We will have minis prepped and ready for painting, perfect for crafters who want a tiny monster friend for spooky season or TTRPG players who need a new addition to their dungeon. Plus, can your mini-monster face off against a vampire duck? We will have rubber duckies to monster-ify as well! No registration is required; walk in while supplies last. The program space is for adults and teens (ages 13+) only. Please browse children's events if you are interested in events for younger ages. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Drop in and build your own monster miniature craft project with other teens and adults.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 18th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Success, Ambition, Sex "One who understands the limits of the good life knows that what eliminates the pains brought on by need and what makes the whole of life perfect is easily obtained, so that there is no need for enterprises that entail the struggle for success." Principal Doctrine 21. "Great abundance is heaped up as the result of brutalizing labor, but a miserable life is the result." Fragment 73. "If there is intense striving after those physical desires that do not lead to pain if unfulfilled, this is because they arise from idle opinion; they fail to be dispelled, not because of their own nature but because of the vain fancies of humankind." Principal Doctrine 30. "Happiness and blessedness do not belong to abundance of riches or exalted position or offices or power, but to freedom from pain and gentleness of feeling and a state of mind that sets limits that are in accordance with nature." Fragment 85. "I learn from your letter that carnal disturbances make you excessively inclined to sexual intercourse. Well, so long as you do not break any laws or disturb well-established conventions or annoy any of your neighbors or wear down your body or use up your funds, you may carry out your own plans as you like. However, it is impossible not to be affected by at least one of these things. Sex never benefited any man, and it's a marvel if it hasn't injured him!" Vatican Sayings 51. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 13 (pp. 137-144) and 16 (pp. 171-179). Some Questions to Discuss: What effect do competitive relations and ambitions have on us as individuals and as a society? What does it mean to be successful for Epicurus? What would be counted as success in our society? How do we reason our understanding of success? Would we agree with Epicurus's argument on sexual desire?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

events.description: Come and prepare for Day of the Dead / Día de los Muertos by learning a few simple make-up techniques that you can do on your own face or someone else's, with Bay Area multi-cultural arts educator Rachel-Anne Palacios. We'll provide supplies to learn and practice, but please come with a clean face. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world.

events.title: Author Event: Book launch for Bruce Overby's latest novel
events.description: Join us for an evening with local writer Bruce Overby (The Cyclone Release and recently released Tristan 4 America) with Geri Spieler (Housewife Assassin, Regina of Warsaw) serving as moderator. Bruce Overby is a fiction writer with particular interest in issues of loss and belonging, family and relationships, the human condition in a technology-driven world, and addiction. His fiction has appeared in Storyglossia, the Green Mountains Review, the Evening Street Review, and the anthology Home of the Brave: Stories in Uniform from Press53. "Bookmarks," the story of a brother's struggle with alcoholism, his love of poetry, and the sometimes disturbing mix of the two, won first prize in the Lorian Hemingway Short Story Competition. Bruce's debut novel, The Cyclone Release, was a finalist in the Blue Moon Novel Competition and is available now from Madville Publishing. His second novel, Tristan 4 America, is forthcoming from Willow River Press in October 2026. Bruce is a graduate of the MFA in Writing Program at Queens University of Charlotte. A San Jose native, Bruce is a member of California Writers Club-SF Peninsula Branch and participated in Rinconada Library's inaugural book fair in April. Books will be available for purchase. Bring your questions!

events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; and legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear Lindsay recount Italian Americans' wartime displacement under Executive Order 9066.
