events.description: The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) are hosting a friendly needle works stitch-in. Come join us from 10 am to 2 pm in the conference room; there are always extra seats! The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) chapter of the American Needlepoint Guild was chartered on March 1, 1986. We meet monthly at the Milpitas Police Department Community Room. At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint. The purpose of the American Needlepoint Guild is for education and cultural development through participation in and encouragement of interest in the art of needlepoint, which is defined as needlework executed by hand with a threaded needle on a readily counted ground. If you would like to find out more about SBN, please join us at one of our meetings or contact us at: sbnangcontact@gmail.com.

events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; and legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7] Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch this documentary tracing a Stasi victim's personal investigation into East Germany's surveillance machine.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a friendly reading and discussion group at the library tackling big questions about how we live and what we value.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard

(There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep these resources on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Hear library staff break down the warning signs of holiday shopping scams before you click buy.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her novel A Hidden Fate about family secrets and genetic foreknowledge.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... Provocative.... Moving.... Beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. EP has recently moved its offices out of New York and California. The new headquarters for all operations is now in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year and currently, Bravo-the Independent Film Channel retains the rights to cablecast the film. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick Mac Arthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary The Panama Deception, examining U.S. military history in Panama.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a discussion group questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence over a shared reading.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Discuss the group's chosen graphic novel with fellow readers age 16 and up at Mitchell Park Library.

events.title: Pageturners: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Bachman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss Michael Chabon's Kavalier & Clay with fellow readers at Pageturners book club.

events.title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
events.description: Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project Humane Kind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Registration required. Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time. As founder of Clorofil, an animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.
events.blurb: Meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and her chicken to learn surprising facts about how chickens see, dream, and recognize faces.

events.title: Native Plant Gardening for Year-round Interest
events.description: One person can make a difference! Come to learn how you can incorporate California native plants in your garden to bring back much-needed pollinators to our urban habitat and provide beauty in your yard. Thousands of plants are native to California, and this talk will focus on selecting native plants for color and interest through all seasons of the year. Enjoy blooms, butterflies, bees, and birds year round! Both new and experienced gardeners are welcome!
events.blurb: Learn how California native plants can bring pollinators and year-round beauty back to your yard.

events.title: LEGO Fun!
events.description: Lots and lots of LEGOs... Seriously, a lot. This program is held every third Sunday of the month at Bascom. Create something cool? We can display a photo of it on the library's LCD TV! Ask staff and we'll take a photo of it. For children and families. Registration recommended but not required. Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards. Lego by Alexander Lowe; Amazing Vehicles by Rona Skene.
events.blurb: Build with a huge pile of LEGO bricks and maybe get your creation displayed on the library TV.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. This week, we'll be celebrating Native American Heritage Month. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children and no previous experience is needed!
events.blurb: Dance, sing, and play instruments with Librarian Celina in a Native American Heritage Month celebration.

All levels of English speaking skills are welcome!

Our quizzes take place from 2-6 PM on the second Sunday of every month, at Mitchell Park Library, Palo Alto. It is free and open to everyone.

events.description: In this workshop folks will learn how to make a festive holiday placemat to decorate your home for the holidays. You should know how to: thread the machine, fill the bobbin, use the backstitch, and understand the various other parts/functions of the sewing machine. Open to teens and adults only.

events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our reading volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud with our volunteer. Please note, this is not a tutoring session. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.

ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Grab supplied materials and build your own monstrous Halloween craft for school-age kids.

events.title: Jack O'Lantern Jamboree!
events.description: We're throwing a Halloween dance party and YOU'RE invited! Children and their families are invited to come decked out in costume and dance with us in the Secret Garden of Children's Library*. We will also have fun crafts and light refreshments. Bring the whole family and join us for this special event! Registration is not required. *In the event of rain, this event will take place in the Treetop Room.
events.blurb: Dance in costume with your family at a Halloween party in the Secret Garden of Children's Library.

events.title: Gentle Yoga / Yoga Relajante
events.description: Discover a soothing practice designed for all bodies and all levels. Gentle Yoga invites you to relax, restore, and feel better from the inside out. Free. No registration required. Bring your own mat. Explora una práctica relajante creada para todos los cuerpos y niveles. El Yoga relajante te invita a restaurarte y reconectar contigo mismo. Gratis. No necesita registrarse. Trae tu propio tapete.
events.blurb: Move through a gentle yoga practice designed for all bodies and levels, offered in English and Spanish.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club
events.description: The ESL Conversation Club is returning to the Milpitas Library! Please join us for this fun sharing experience. Improve your English listening and speaking skills and learn about other cultures in a supportive environment. This program is for adults aged 18 and older who speak basic English. We will be holding ongoing weekly meetings in the Program Room on the first floor. We welcome drop-ins!
events.blurb: Practice your English speaking and listening skills and swap stories with others at Milpitas Library's ESL Conversation Club.

events.title: 1K Books Stuffed Animal Sleepover
events.description: Join the 1,000 Books Before Kindergarten Stuffed Animal Sleepover at San José Public Library! Families with kids ages 0–5 can drop off a stuffed animal for a night of library fun. Pick up your furry friend the next day with a keepsake photo and "sleepover report." Free. No registration required. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Drop off your child's stuffed animal for an overnight library adventure and pick up a keepsake photo.

events.title: LEGO Fridays!
events.description: We have the LEGOs! Bring your imagination and build something fun! LEGOs will stay at the library, so be sure to snap a pic of your creation! In addition to being a great way to introduce the engineering and art concepts of STEAM, playing with LEGOs supports early childhood development because children engage in problem solving, teamwork, self-confidence, and creativity!
events.blurb: College Terrace Library supplies the LEGOs every Friday, so bring your ideas and build something worth photographing.

If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring your baby in a carrier and learn a dance routine set to popular tunes.

events.title: Resume Review & Interview Preparation
events.description: A well-crafted resume is vital for standing out to potential employers. Our volunteer will help you learn the essential elements of a successful resume and prepare for interviews. Gain expert tips on highlighting your accomplishments, showcasing transferable skills, and mastering the STAR framework to ace your next interview. *No registration required* #sjplworkscareer
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help polishing your resume and practicing interview answers with a volunteer coach.

events.title: LEGO Club!
events.description: Come join us every Sunday for LEGO Club! We have tons of LEGO bricks for you to build and explore! Duplo bricks are also available for our younger friends. Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a LEGO Challenge! Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards.
events.blurb: Build with a huge collection of Lego and Duplo bricks and try a librarian-issued Lego Challenge.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: Friday Fun: DIY Lip Scrub
events.description: Join us every Friday at the Willow Glen Branch Library for a fun activity for kids. Activities may include arts & crafts, special performances or workshops, and board or video games. Note: 2nd Friday of every month is free play with Legos! This day we'll be learning how to make our own sugar lip scrub. All supplies will be provided. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Make your own lip scrub in this week's Friday Fun craft session for kids.

events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines
events.description: Volunteer away your library fines at a rate of $20 per hour while helping the library maintain a clean and welcoming environment. Requirements: Must be able to commit to the 60-minute session. Anyone under the age of 13 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardian. No experience or special skills necessary. The library will provide supplies. Registration required.
events.blurb: Work off your library fines by volunteering for a 60-minute shift helping keep the library tidy.

events.title: Tea Time & Crossword Puzzle
events.description: Join us for tea, refreshments, music, and a crossword puzzle to solve collaboratively! Hot tea will be served October through March, and iced tea April through September. This event is held every third Monday of the month at Bascom Library in Study Room 2. No registration required. All ages welcome. This program is generously funded by Friends of Bascom Library.
events.blurb: Sip tea and solve a crossword puzzle together with fellow regulars at Bascom Library.

events.title: Knitting / Crocheting / Tatting / Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, tatting, or bobbin lace project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the community room.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.

events.title: Friday Fun: Halloween Celebration
events.description: Celebrate Halloween with us at Tully library. Many fun activities await you including: Books Giveaway; Goody Bags & Candies Giveaway (while supplies last); Face Painting; Balloon Artist; Arts & Crafts; Games & Prizes; Photo Booth; Grand Prize Drawings. Free. No registration required. Explore more Friday Fun at Tully Community Branch events on our events calendar.
events.blurb: Enjoy face painting, balloon art, games, and goody bags at Tully Library's Halloween celebration.

events.title: Village Square Homework Club
events.description: Need room to get homework done and work on class projects? Join us at the Village Square Homework Club. Basic school supplies and snacks are provided. Volunteers are available to help with homework assignments as well. Teens are also welcome to come and work on their school assignments. This program is supported by Friends of Village Square Branch Library.
events.blurb: Get homework done and work on class projects with volunteer help at the Homework Club.

events.title: Game Zone
events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics? Or maybe you'd like to sink the 8 ball at a game of pool? Join us in the Teen Room at the Hillview Branch Library if you want to play video, board, and card games, play some pool, or just hang out! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play video, board, and card games in the Teen Room, or challenge friends to a game of pool.

events.title: Freaky Friday Night Flicks
events.description: Watch some Halloween classics at your library! Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid-back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. This program is for teens (ages 13-18). October 16th: Beetlejuice (1988); October 23rd: The Addams Family (1991); October 30th: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).
events.blurb: Watch Halloween classics at the library with friends, popcorn and candy provided for teens 13-18.

events.title: Reading to Children with Aysha
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Read one-on-one or in a small group with volunteer Aysha to build reading confidence and love of books.

events.title: Crochet Together
events.description: Crochet Together with the Mt Pleasant Neighborhood Library! Crochet Together is a volunteer-run event teaching participants how to crochet. Participants are welcome to bring their own materials. For children interested in crochet, the recommended age is 10 years old and older. Children who are 10 years old and younger must be accompanied by parents.
events.blurb: Learn to crochet with volunteer instructors, bringing your own materials if you have them.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.title: Arts & Crafts Fun
events.description: Our partner, Budding Leaders, is hosting arts and crafts classes for ages 4+ with adult help, 8+ solo. We will supply materials and samples and help you create beautiful artwork. Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.attendanceNote: Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.blurb: Make arts and crafts projects with supplied materials at Calabazas Library's kids craft class.

events.title: Mandarin Storytime
events.description: Join us for fun stories, rhymes, fingerplays and songs in Mandarin! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and songs performed in Mandarin at this Saratoga Library storytime.

events.title: Board Game Day
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Join us for a volunteer-led hour of family-friendly board games on the third Sunday of every month. The library will have games on hand, but participants are also welcome to bring their own games to play at the library. Please bring games that are appropriate for all ages. Light refreshments will be served. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play family-friendly board games with other visitors at East SJ Carnegie Library, or bring your own.

events.title: Library Tech Help
events.description: Do you have a question about your computer? About email? About your phone? Visit the Alum Rock Tech Center to get help from a librarian or watch short videos about using everyday technology. You're welcome to bring your own device. The librarian will do their best to help troubleshoot basic issues. Attendance is first-come, first-served.
events.attendanceNote: Attendance is first-come, first-served.
events.blurb: Bring your device to the Alum Rock Tech Center and get one-on-one help from a librarian.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.
events.blurb: Sit down with Mayor Kitty Moore and raise whatever's on your mind at this informal monthly chat.

events.title: Guided Meditation & Yoga for Wellness and Stress Relief
events.description: Free in-person meditation and yoga session. Simple standing or chair-based stretches (no mats required). Practice is designed to improve focus, emotional balance, and inner calm. Presented by Dhyan Foundation, dedicated to promoting physical, mental and spiritual well-being through authentic yogic practices and community education.
events.blurb: Try guided meditation and simple standing or chair-based stretches led by the Dhyan Foundation.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer and it will be held under the Read to Children sign, within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Watch kids read to a volunteer in a small group under the Read to Children sign at Berryessa Library.

events.title: Friends of the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library Book Sale
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Choose from a large collection of slightly used books for all ages and interests. Come support your local library branch and find new literary treasures for yourself. Cash and credit cards will be accepted. Proceeds go toward funding library programs and supplies. Hosted by the Friends of the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library.
events.blurb: Shop a large collection of used books at the King Library's fundraising book sale, cash or card accepted.

events.title: Jewelry Making for Adults
events.description: Get crafty and relax at a jewelry-making night just for adults. Supplies will be available to create whatever you like. Make something for yourself or a gift for a friend. Better yet, bring a friend! Not sure where to start? We'll have project ideas and examples to help you get inspired. Come be creative, unwind, and have fun.
events.blurb: Adults make their own jewelry using provided supplies and project ideas at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Game On at the Library
events.description: Join us every Sunday at 1:00 p.m. at the Joyce Ellington Branch for a fun afternoon of board games! Choose from our large selection of games, including exciting new favorites and classic games that are fun for all ages. Bring your family and friends, roll the dice, and enjoy some friendly competition! No registration required.
events.blurb: Choose from a large selection of board games and play with family and friends at the library.

events.title: Crafter Dark: Halloween / Fall Keychains
events.description: This event happens on the third Wednesday of every month. This month we are making Halloween or Fall keychains or phone charms. This craft uses beads, pliers, and wire to create colorful and personalized accessories. All supplies and tools are provided by the library. There is some fine motor skill required for this craft.
events.blurb: Make Halloween or fall-themed keychains and phone charms using beads, pliers, and wire.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Excel Basics
events.description: New to Microsoft Excel? This beginner-friendly workshop will introduce you to the essentials, including navigating spreadsheets, entering and formatting data, creating simple formulas, and organizing information. Get comfortable with Excel and build the skills you need to confidently tackle everyday tasks. Free.
events.blurb: Learn to navigate spreadsheets, enter data, and build simple formulas in this beginner Excel workshop.

events.title: Board Game Zone
events.description: Join us every Sunday between 2:00 - 4:00 PM at the Seven Trees Library to play fun board games! We have a large selection to choose from, including new games and classic games that people of all ages can enjoy. No registration required. Thanks to the Friends of the Seven Trees Library for making this possible!
events.blurb: Pick from a large selection of new and classic board games to play with all ages welcome.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: All are welcome—from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. Bring your own project or start a new one as we refine our skills and discuss all things crochet. A volunteer is available to provide instructions, and offer advice to beginners. Tools and supplies are provided. The minimum age is six years old.
events.blurb: Bring your own crochet project or start something new with guidance from a volunteer instructor.

events.title: Basic English Level 1
events.description: Learn the basics of English in an inclusive and welcoming environment! You will: Learn basic vocabulary; Understand simple grammar; Read simple texts and write basic sentences. Lớp này sẽ được giảng dạy bởi một giáo viên có khả năng song ngữ Anh-Việt. Free. Registration requested, but not required.
events.blurb: Build basic English vocabulary and grammar and practice reading and writing simple sentences with a bilingual teacher.

events.title: Piano Basics & Music Principles
events.description: Participants will learn the basics of playing piano and be introduced to music notation and staff lines. Instructors will bring their own keyboards. You're welcome to bring your keyboard if you have one, but it is not required. First-come, first-served. Limited to 15 slots. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.attendanceNote: First come first serve. Limited to 15 slots.
events.blurb: Learn basic piano technique and music notation on a keyboard, with instructors ready to teach beginners.

events.title: LEGO Engineering Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Come join us at East SJ Carnegie Branch Library for our LEGO Club! Participate in a weekly engineering challenge or make whatever you want! Important: This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build and tackle a weekly LEGO engineering challenge or create your own design at this club.

events.title: Learn English: Holiday Fun!
events.description: Are you an adult learning English? Join us for a casual gathering with fellow English learners where you can play games, make holiday cards, learn about American winter traditions, and enjoy holiday music! Registration is optional. If you register, you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Practice English with other adult learners while playing games and making holiday cards at this casual gathering.

events.title: Nameless Anime Club
events.description: Do you enjoy anime and manga? Join Edenvale Branch Library's Nameless Anime Club! Enjoy classic anime from the past, new series from today, and make new friends! Participants are welcome to drop in anytime during our program. We hope to see you there! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop by Edenvale Library to watch anime old and new and meet fellow fans at Nameless Anime Club.

events.title: Video Game Tournament
events.description: Rev your engines and race to the finish line! Join us at the library for a fun-filled Nintendo Switch tournament featuring Mario Kart. Compete against fellow racers, show off your skills, and see who can take home the victory. All skill levels are welcome! Recommended for ages 7+.
events.blurb: Race opponents in a Nintendo Switch Mario Kart tournament at the library.

events.title: Chess for Beginners
events.description: Join us for beginner & intermediate chess! Whether you're brand new to the game or looking to sharpen your skills, you're invited to learn and play chess in a relaxed, supportive environment. Walk-ins are welcome, and all materials are provided. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn chess moves and strategy or sharpen your game against other beginners and intermediate players.

events.title: The Peaceful Poets
events.description: The Peaceful Poets are a Milpitas-based group of writers and appreciators of poetry. They welcome all who are interested. The meetings are free. The group meets the last Thursday of every month (except November and December) at 5:30 PM in the Milpitas Library Conference Room.
events.blurb: Share and discuss poetry with fellow writers at the Peaceful Poets' meeting in the Milpitas Library conference room.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration is not required but you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: ArtSEE Expression: Thankfulness Cards
events.description: Join ArtSEE Expression's very own Sharvi in this teen-led program where you will design custom thankfulness cards! Participants will be using pressed flowers, paints, construction paper, and decorative accents to explore their creativity through this unique art activity.
events.blurb: Design custom thankfulness cards using pressed flowers, paints, and decorative accents in this teen-led session.

events.title: Basic English 2 Class
events.description: For learners with limited ability in English, students will practice speaking using guided dialogues to help them navigate in the community they live in. The class will review topical grammar and vocabulary as needed. The program is drop-in and free. No registration needed.
events.blurb: Practice English speaking through guided dialogues and review grammar and vocabulary for everyday life.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Juliana on Saturday mornings at 10:30 a.m. for Family Storytime at Mitchell Park Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! Follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and read along with Librarian Juliana at this Saturday morning family storytime.

events.title: Vietnamese Class for Kids
events.description: Are you between the ages of 5 and 12, and do you want to learn Vietnamese? Tully Branch Library will be offering a class for children to learn basic Vietnamese language, grammar, spelling, dictation, writing, and reading. In-person registration is required at Tully Library.
events.blurb: Learn basic Vietnamese vocabulary, grammar, and writing in a class designed for kids ages 5-12.

events.title: ESL Writing Club
events.description: Practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Sessions will cover simple sentence structures and basic grammar, building up to writing a simple paragraph. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice basic English sentence writing and grammar with a tutor in a relaxed small-group setting for adults.

events.title: Teen Coffeehouse
events.description: Teens: join us for Coffeehouse, Saratoga's open mic night organized by the Teen Advisory Board and the Youth Commission. Teen performers: sign up at tinyurl.com/TABcoffeehouse to perform. Music, singing, dancing, poetry, stand-up comedy - show your talent!
events.blurb: Watch teens perform music, poetry, and comedy at Saratoga Library's open mic Coffeehouse night.

events.title: Chess Club for Kids
events.description: Come learn to play chess, or just play a game! This is an informal and welcoming program for kids up to age 12 and their families. Chess Club meets every Monday. Please check the website event listing for possible date cancellations and library holidays.
events.blurb: Learn chess moves or jump into a casual game with other kids and families.

events.title: Halloween Karaoke Night
events.description: Join us for a night of hauntingly good tunes, thrilling performances, and ghoulish fun! Dress up, sing loud, and let the spirits of music take over. Open to all ages! Registration is not required, but if you do register, you'll receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Sing your favorite tunes in costume at a Halloween-themed karaoke night open to all ages.

events.title: Friendly Stitchers
events.description: Do you enjoy--or want to learn--cross stitch and embroidery? Join our weekly stitching social! Bring your own project of any kind or stitch our small sample project while enjoying the company of fellow needlecrafters. Drop in. No sign-ups required.
events.blurb: Bring your own cross stitch or embroidery project and stitch alongside fellow needlecrafters.

events.title: Family Games: Cards & Board Games
events.description: Children, teens, and their families are invited to play a selection of board games and card games. The games included will be a mix of strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games. Come together to have fun with friends and family!
events.blurb: Gather with family and friends to play a mix of strategy, luck-based, and educational board and card games.

events.title: Hands Only CPR/AED & Choking Relief Training
events.description: A 90-minute informational workshop taught by Santa Clara County Fire Department staff covering hands-only CPR, AED use, and choking relief for adults, children, and infants; costs $15 and participants receive a free pocket mask and first aid kit.
events.blurb: Learn hands-only CPR, AED use, and choking relief from Santa Clara County Fire Department staff.

events.title: Winter Storytime Spectacular!
events.description: Join our Storytime librarians for a Winter Storytime Spectacular! Bring home a take-and-make craft kit while supplies last. Follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Catch stories and songs with the storytime librarians, then take home a winter craft kit.

events.title: ELL Conversation Club for Beginners
events.description: Come and practice speaking English with a friendly group in the library. We will practice: Vocabulary for everyday activities; Listening skills; Reading skills; Speaking skills. Free. No registration is required. For adults ages 18 and over.
events.blurb: Practice everyday English vocabulary, listening, and speaking with a friendly beginner group at the library.

events.title: Coloring for Adults
events.description: Coloring sheets and pencils are provided every Monday afternoon from 1:00-6:30 PM in the lobby of Bascom Library. Relax and explore your creativity with this great activity! All ages welcome to participate. No registration required.
events.blurb: Grab provided coloring sheets and pencils and unwind in the Bascom Library lobby on Monday afternoons.

events.description: Boost your child's academic confidence! Students in grades K-6 can receive free homework assistance at Saratoga Library. Sessions are led by enthusiastic college volunteer tutors who can help clarify concepts and reinforce learning.

events.description: Are you interested in playing and learning chess? If so, you are invited to the Village Square Branch Library to come and learn to play chess at the beginner and intermediate levels. No registration required. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.blurb: Learn chess basics or sharpen your intermediate game at this walk-in club, no registration needed.

events.title: STEAM Lab Saturday: Zombie Juice!
events.description: Make spooky "Zombie Juice" as you watch dry ice turn from a solid to a gas, creating bubbling carbon dioxide and creepy fog that brings a glove-hand to life! Registration required for children only. Adults do not need to register.
events.blurb: Watch dry ice turn solid to gas as you make bubbling, fog-filled Zombie Juice and animate a glove hand.

events.title: Basic English Level 0
events.description: Learn the basics of English in an inclusive and welcoming environment! You will: Learn basic vocabulary; Understand simple grammar; Read simple texts and write basic sentences. Free. Registration requested, but not required.
events.blurb: Learn basic English vocabulary, simple grammar, and beginner reading and writing in a welcoming classroom setting.

events.title: Make It Mondays: Spin Art Pumpkins
events.description: Join us every Monday for arts and crafts at the library! Each week will feature a different activity that focuses on building creativity, social-emotional, and school readiness skills through art. All supplies will be provided!
events.blurb: Make a spin art pumpkin craft and build creativity skills at this weekly Monday art session.

events.title: Hidden Treasures
events.address: Cupertino Senior Center, 21251 Stevens Creek Boulevard, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Join us at the Senior Center for Hidden Treasures! With hundreds of items to choose from, this event is the perfect opportunity to discover unique antiques, artwork, handknits, toys, glassware, housewares, jewelry, and more.
events.blurb: Browse hundreds of donated antiques, artwork, toys, and housewares at the Senior Center's Hidden Treasures sale.

events.title: STEM Club: Witches' Cauldron Slime
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Drop in and join us every Monday from 4 PM-5 PM for an evening of STEM-related family fun! This club is intended for ages 5-10, but all families are welcome. Free. No registration required. 10/19 - Witches' Cauldron Slime
events.blurb: Drop in with the family to mix up witch's cauldron slime at this weekly STEM club.

events.title: Huge Paperback Book Sale

events.description: Join us at the Village Square Branch Library for a fun-filled event to celebrate and highlight the diversity of people and cultures around us. Come celebrate Diwali with arts, crafts, and snacks! While supplies last.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with crafts, arts, and snacks at Village Square Branch Library.

events.title: Video Game Zone
events.description: Have fun and compete with others in a variety of popular games on Nintendo Switch, including Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate! Open to teens and pre-teens. No registration required.
events.blurb: Compete in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on Nintendo Switch at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: Itty-Bitty Halloween S'Booktacular (For Ages 0-6)
events.description: Join us for not-so-scary activities, a costume parade, and trick-or-treating in the library. Wear your spookiest costume and join the fun! This program is for children ages 0-6 and their caregivers.
events.blurb: Join a costume parade and trick-or-treating in the library for a not-so-scary Halloween event.

events.title: ArtSEE Expression: Ornament Painting
events.description: Join ArtSEE Expression's very own Sharvi in this teen-led program where you will design custom ornaments! Participants will use paints, glitter, and fun textures to create one-of-a-kind decorations.
events.blurb: Design one-of-a-kind ornaments with paints, glitter, and textures in this teen-led art session.

events.title: CSCS William C. Dement Seminar Series: "Targeted, physiology-informed therapy for sleep apnea: Novel pharmacotherapy and beyond" with Danny Eckert, Ph.D.
events.description: Please join us for this month's Center for Sleep and Circadian Sciences William C. Dement Seminar Series!
events.blurb: Log on to hear Danny Eckert, PhD, present new physiology-informed pharmacotherapy approaches to sleep apnea.

events.title: MACLA Presents: Diana Gameros in Concert Ft. Magik*Magik

events.blurb: Hear Diana Gameros in concert with the Magik*Magik String Quartet at MACLA.

events.description: Free. Offered in person, in English or Spanish. Would you like to find out more about computers? Learn at your own pace! ¿Te gustaría aprender más sobre computadoras? ¡Aprende a tu propio ritmo!
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help learning computers at your own pace, in English or Spanish.

events.title: Cbd 2026: Mindfulness, Embodied Self-awareness, and Disembodied AI with Shaun Gallagher, PhD, Hon DPhil
events.description: Dr. Gallagher will discuss the "4E Cognition"—Embodied, Embedded, Extended, Enactive Cognition—approaches to inquiries into questions of self-awareness.

events.title: Concert: Music at Kohl Mansion presents Escher String Quartet
events.description: Now in our fourth year of partnership with Music at Kohl Mansion, we proudly present the Escher String Quartet. The Escher String Quartet has established itself as one of the most accomplished chamber ensembles of its generation. Formed in New York City in 2005, and named after the Dutch graphic artist M.C. Escher, the quartet is celebrated for performances that combine technical brilliance, interpretive insight, and a distinctive ensemble sound. The group serves as Artists of the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and has earned international recognition for its commitment to both the core string quartet repertoire and contemporary music. The quartet has appeared at many of the world's leading concert halls and festivals, including London's Wigmore Hall, Amsterdam's Concertgebouw, the Kennedy Center, Paris's Auditorium du Louvre, and major chamber music festivals throughout North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. Praised by critics for their precision, warmth, and expressive depth, the Escher String Quartet has received numerous honors, including the prestigious Avery Fisher Career Grant and Lincoln Center's Martin E. Segal Award. The ensemble's critically acclaimed recording projects include the complete string quartets of Alexander Zemlinsky and Felix Mendelssohn and more. Through its adventurous programming and consistently compelling performances, the Escher String Quartet continues to be recognized as one of the leading chamber ensembles on the international stage.
events.blurb: Hear the Escher String Quartet perform chamber music at Music at Kohl Mansion.

events.title: Am I Being Tracked? A Guide to Digital Privacy
events.description: Registration is required. Every click, search, and scroll leaves a trail, but how much of your life is actually being monitored, and by whom? In "Am I Being Tracked?", we take a hype-free look at the modern tracking ecosystem. First, we'll debunk some myths around online privacy. Next, we'll reframe how you think about digital privacy, shifting the goal from "total invisibility" to smart data management. Finally, you'll get a practical checklist of steps you can take right now to gain control over your personal data. About the Presenter: Iman Saleh is a local Mountain View mom and a privacy professional with more than 24 years of experience in big tech and academia. She holds a Ph.D. in Software Engineering and is recognized as a Fellow of Information Privacy by the International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP).
events.blurb: Learn how online tracking actually works and hear the myths around digital privacy debunked in this online session.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Cherie Dimaline
events.description: Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls. Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline's expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and VenCo. About the Author: Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by Time magazine one of the Best YA Books of All Time and won the Governor General's Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel VenCo debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (AILA Honor Book, Aurora Award winner, Crime Writers Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General's Award Finalist). Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for Marvel, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.

events.title: Online Author Talk: E. Lockhart
events.description: Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed. But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be. When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She's running from a glittering life she won't speak about. He's hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage. One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever. Ask Lockhart questions live! About the Author: Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the Liars novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.
events.blurb: Hear E. Lockhart discuss We Were Liars and get a preview of her new thriller, The Pools.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Paul Vigna
events.description: Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS.
events.blurb: Hear journalist Paul Vigna discuss how money evolved into a stand-in for morality and virtue.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Pyet DeSpain
events.description: Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet DeSpain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay's hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking. Pyet DeSpain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine. Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as: Three Sisters Salad; Bison and Sweet Corn Soup; Fry Bread; Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake; Corn Silk and Honey Tea; Wojapi BBQ Sauce. Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes; it is a movement giving voice to Indigenous culture, histories, and foodways through the universal language of food. Register for this event today and learn how to work with nature in your own kitchen. About the Author: Pyet—short for her inherited Native American name, Pyetwetmokwe—is a member of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation and an award-winning global private chef. She made history as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Next Level Chef and was named one of Entrepreneur Magazine's Top 25 Private Chefs in Los Angeles. Her work is centered on uplifting Indigenous foodways within the culinary industry while advocating for a more sustainable and sovereign food system for Indigenous peoples.
events.blurb: Hear chef Pyet DeSpain talk about her cookbook Rooted in Fire online.
